paper_metadata.title: Efficient DCQO Algorithm within the Impulse Regime for Portfolio Optimization

summary: The paper introduces digitized‑counterdiabatic quantum optimization (DCQO) for portfolio optimization and demonstrates a 2.5×–40× reduction in circuit depth compared with QAOA or digitized adiabatic evolution. On a 20‑asset problem executed on the IonQ Aria trapped‑ion device (20 qubits, 5000 shots), DCQO achieved an approximation ratio ≈0.54 with only 7 Trotter steps (effectively 1 after gate cutoff), while the hybrid h‑DCQO ansatz matched 5‑layer QAOA performance using only a single layer.

experiments.description: Purely quantum digitized-counterdiabatic quantum optimization (DCQO) for portfolio optimization, benchmarked against finite-time digitized-adiabatic evolution and evaluated on a 20-asset real-market instance and on random Ising spin-glass instances up to 20 qubits.

algorithm.variant: digitized-counterdiabatic quantum optimization (DCQO) in the impulse regime
algorithm.ansatz: Trotterized CD-only circuit with Ry, Rzy, and Ryz blocks; first-order nested-commutator CD term
algorithm.hyperparameters.Trotter_steps_CD_only: 6 for the random‑instance benchmark in Fig. 3; 7 Trotter steps used for the 20‑asset portfolio experiment (reduced to 1 step after gate cutoff)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per binary asset-selection variable xi ∈ {0,1}; Ising encoding of portfolio optimization / spin-glass Hamiltonian
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize Σ_i x_i e_i − θ Σ_{i,j} x_i x_j c_ij subject to Σ_i x_i ≤ B; equivalently unconstrained objective with penalty term θ3(Σ_i x_i − B)^2
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: budget constraint absorbed into penalty term θ3(Σ_i x_i − B)^2; gate cutoff used to omit small-angle rotations in impulse regime
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_f = Σ_i h_i Z_i + Σ_{i<j} J_ij Z_i Z_j

problem_instance.description: 20-asset portfolio optimization using real stock data; also benchmarked on 1000 random all-to-all Ising spin-glass instances with 10 to 20 assets/qubits
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Historical stock prices used to build coefficients of the Ising Hamiltonian; no further preprocessing details reported
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulation on 1000 random Ising instances; portfolio instance evaluated by approximation ratio r(avg) and energy distributions; hardware run with 5000 shots

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise with reported average gate errors (≈0.06% single‑qubit, ≈0.6% two‑qubit) and systematic errors mitigated by debiasing

implementation_details.classical_solver: COBYLA for hybrid optimization; simulation and hardware execution via Amazon Braket
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Coefficients h_i and J_ij computed from Markowitz formulation using historical stock prices; gate-angle cutoff applied to omit rotations with angle < 0.1
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Approximation ratio r(avg) computed from measured energy distributions; debiased results compared to raw hardware and simulation

speedup_claims.conditions: 20-asset portfolio instance; 7 DCQO steps reduced to 1 effective step after gate cutoff; depth-per-step for DCQO is twice that of the adiabatic baseline
speedup_claims.caveats: Reported as circuit-depth reduction, not runtime speedup; based on gate cutoff and step-count comparison.

speedup_claims.conditions: 1000 random Ising spin-glass instances up to 20 qubits; fixed circuit depths
speedup_claims.caveats: Described as an increase in approximation ratio, not a computational speedup.

speedup_claims.conditions: Portfolio optimization on 20 assets; impulse-regime DCQO and h-DCQO comparisons
speedup_claims.caveats: Range aggregates multiple comparisons; exact factor depends on baseline and whether gate cutoff is applied.

complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: Circuit depth reduced by factors of 2.5 to 40 versus QAOA / digitized-adiabatic baselines

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not specified; experiments limited to ≤20 qubits and shallow circuits on trapped‑ion hardware
limiting_factors: No comparison with state‑of‑the‑art classical portfolio optimization solvers
Only approximation‑ratio comparisons among quantum algorithms
NISQ noise and limited circuit depth

notes: 20 qubits and IonQ Aria are explicitly stated.

Circuit depth is reported comparatively (e.g., 7 DCQO steps reduce to 1 after gate cutoff; 80 steps for digitized-adiabatic baseline; 12/4/6 Trotter steps for benchmark comparisons), but no single absolute transpiled depth is given.
The experiment includes both simulation and hardware execution; hardware type is real_qpu_trapped_ion because the paper explicitly says IonQ trapped-ion quantum computer / Aria.
The algorithm family is mapped to other-gate-based because DCQO is a gate-based digital quantum algorithm and does not fit the closed-set families more specifically.
The paper does not claim quantum advantage over classical algorithms; it compares DCQO only against other quantum methods (digitized adiabatic evolution and QAOA).
Experiments run on a 20‑qubit IonQ Aria device, which is far below scales where classical combinatorial optimization becomes challenging.

experiments.description: Hybrid digitized-counterdiabatic quantum optimization (h-DCQO) for portfolio optimization, compared against QAOA at different depths and executed on IonQ hardware with and without debiasing.

algorithm.ansatz: CD-only variational ansatz with one parameter per CD term; layers built from Y + YZ + ZY operator blocks
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Parameters learned locally before final hardware execution; specific initialization not reported

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per binary asset-selection variable xi ∈ {0,1}; Ising encoding of portfolio optimization
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize Σ_i x_i e_i − θ Σ_{i,j} x_i x_j c_ij subject to Σ_i x_i ≤ B; penalty-form unconstrained objective used for Ising mapping
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: budget penalty term θ3(Σ_i x_i − B)^2; no gate-angle cutoff applied in h-DCQO
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_f = Σ_i h_i Z_i + Σ_{i<j} J_ij Z_i Z_j

problem_instance.description: 20-asset real-market portfolio optimization instance; hardware results reported for h-DCQO and compared to QAOA baselines
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Historical stock prices used to derive Hamiltonian coefficients; no additional preprocessing details reported
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Energy distributions and mean-based approximation ratio r(avg); hardware run with 5000 shots; comparison to QAOA p=1 and p=5

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Local parameter learning before hardware execution; Hamiltonian coefficients derived from market data
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Approximation ratio r(avg) from measured energy distributions; comparison of mitigated vs unmitigated hardware and simulation

speedup_claims.conditions: 20-asset portfolio instance; h-DCQO p=1 compared with QAOA p=5
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a reduction in variational layers, not a proven runtime speedup.

speedup_claims.conditions: Reported comparison where h-DCQO depth per layer is twice QAOA depth per layer
speedup_claims.caveats: Depth reduction is relative to the reported QAOA comparison; no absolute depth given.

speedup_claims.conditions: Portfolio optimization on 20 assets; overall paper claim
speedup_claims.caveats: Aggregate claim across multiple baselines and settings.

complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: One-layer h-DCQO matches five-layer QAOA, implying 5x fewer layers and 2.5x lower circuit depth than QAOA in the reported comparison

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not analyzed; results restricted to 20‑qubit hardware experiments and simulation comparisons with QAOA
limiting_factors: Variational training with classical optimizer (COBYLA) introduces classical overhead
Comparison only against QAOA rather than classical portfolio solvers
Noise gap between simulation (r≈0.73) and hardware (r≈0.58)

notes: IonQ Aria hardware and 20 qubits are explicitly reported.
The paper reports p = 1 layer for h-DCQO and compares against QAOA p = 1 and p = 5; no absolute transpiled depth is given.
COBYLA and max 200 iterations are explicitly stated for the hybrid optimization routine.
The algorithm family is hybrid because the paper describes a quantum-classical variational optimization loop.
The paper demonstrates circuit‑depth compression relative to QAOA (1‑layer h‑DCQO ≈ 5‑layer QAOA) but does not claim superiority over classical optimization methods.
Hardware experiments remain at small NISQ scale.
